def solve_cvrp(instance):

    customers = set(instance["customer_ids"])
    demands = instance["demands"]
    capacity = instance["capacity"]

    vehicle_hint = instance.get("vehicle_count_hint", len(customers))

    cust_list = sorted(customers)
    n = len(cust_list)

    def route_cost(route):
        if not route:
            return 0
        d = matrix[depot][route[0]] + matrix[route[-1]][depot]
        for i in range(len(route) - 1):
            d += matrix[route[i]][route[i + 1]]
        return d

    def total_cost(routes):
        return sum(route_cost(r) for r in routes)

    # --- Clarke-Wright savings construction with deterministic merges ---
    # Start with each customer in its own route
    routes = [[i] for i in cust_list]
    route_of = {}
    for idx, r in enumerate(routes):
        route_of[r[0]] = idx
    load_of = [demands[r[0]] for r in routes]

    # Precompute savings list deterministically using nearest_neighbors if available
    nn = instance.get("nearest_neighbors", {})  # keys maybe string
    # Determine candidate pairs: for each i, consider neighbors of i (or all if absent)
    candidates = []
    for i in cust_list:
        neigh = None
        if nn:
            key = str(i)
            if key in nn:
                neigh = nn[key]
            elif isinstance(list(nn.keys())[0] if nn else None, str):
                # try generic
                neigh = nn.get(str(i), None)
        if neigh is None:
            neigh = cust_list
        # limit to avoid O(n^2) blowups
        # deterministic cap: based on instance size
        cap = 40 if n > 180 else 70 if n > 120 else 90
        cnt = 0
        for j in neigh:

                continue
            # only consider i<j to avoid duplicates
            if i < j:
                s = matrix[depot][i] + matrix[depot][j] - matrix[i][j]
                candidates.append((s, i, j))
            cnt += 1
            if cnt >= cap:
                break

    candidates.sort(key=lambda x: (-(x[0]), x[1], x[2]))

    def find_end_positions():
        # for each route index, keep head and tail and their customer
        head = {}
        tail = {}
        for rid, r in enumerate(routes):
            if not r:
                continue
            head[rid] = r[0]
            tail[rid] = r[-1]
        return head, tail

    # Merge only when i is tail of its route and j is head of its route (or swapped via ordered pair)
    head, tail = find_end_positions()
    alive = [True] * len(routes)
    active_route_count = len(routes)

            ri, rj = rj, ri

        # update route_of for nodes in merged route deterministically (only for nodes of rj)

        return d

        neigh = None
        if nn:
            key = str(i)
            if key in nn:
                neigh = nn[key]
            elif isinstance(list(nn.keys())[0] if nn else None, str):
                # try generic
                neigh = nn.get(str(i), None)
        if neigh is None:
            neigh = cust_list

        # deterministic cap: based on instance size

        cnt = 0

            if j == i or j not in customers:
                continue

            if i < j:
                s = matrix[depot][i] + matrix[depot][j] - matrix[i][j]
                candidates.append((s, i, j))
            cnt += 1

                break

    def find_end_positions():

        head = {}
        tail = {}
        for rid, r in enumerate(routes):
            if not r:
                continue
            head[rid] = r[0]
            tail[rid] = r[-1]
        return head, tail

            continue

            routes[ri].extend(routes[rj])
        # orientation 2
        elif tail.get(rj) == j and head.get(ri) == i:
            routes[rj].extend(routes[ri])
